findings.summary: The CHANGELOG timings differ slightly from this snapshot's run, as expected for figures from a single run.
findings.evidence: The CHANGELOG has 1.731 s and 0.145 s; my run printed 1.678 s and 0.153 s. Both are labelled as one-run fixture figures that vary by machine.

summary: The change does what the request asks. `run_check` in crates/athena-gate/src/attribution.rs has two modes, Incremental and FullReplay, and a `CHECK_VERSION`. An incremental run reads the newest checkpoint and judges only main's commits and the records added since it. It falls back to a full replay and states why when there is no checkpoint, the version differs, or the checkpoint names a commit not on main. A full replay adds a CheckpointDisagrees finding when the checkpoint names a commit the replay fails or one not on main. A checkpoint is written with the records writer only after a clean pass with no pending commit. `check --attribution` writes one, and so does `land` after its landing record. Nothing is written when CI is set, with `--no-checkpoint`, or off main. Every run prints the mode, seconds and counts, as text and as JSON. In CI the token stays `contents: read`; pushes run the incremental check and the weekly schedule runs `--full-replay`. I ran every planned demonstration and all passed. The 200-landing fixture printed a 1.678 s full replay (200 commits, 400 records) and a 0.153 s incremental run (1 commit, 2 records), measured in this snapshot. The CHANGELOG quotes 1.731 s and 0.145 s, labelled as fixture figures, and says the timing on this repository is taken after landing. There are only minor gaps: the `land` wiring in `run()` is tested through its helper, not end to end, and history.rs was listed as a deliverable but needed no change.
